1.0.0.en: This verse was explained in the introduction, and it shows the following:

1.0.1.en: 1- The name of the prophet, Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah.

1.0.3.en: 3- His birthplace, which was the village of Anathoth in the tribe of Benjamin.

1.1.0.en: Jeremiah began his prophecy in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah the son of Amon, who was king over the kingdom of Judah, whose capital was Jerusalem and which included the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin. It is called the southern kingdom, as was mentioned in the introduction.

1.2.0.en: The prophecy continued from the days of Jehoiakim the king, the son of Josiah, until Zedekiah the king, the last king of Judah, in the eleventh year of whose reign the captivity took place. The other kings who reigned during the period of the prophecy are not mentioned, because they reigned only for short periods; all this was explained in the introduction.

1.3.0.en: The word of God began to Jeremiah, informing him that he was chosen for the ministry even before he was formed in his mother's womb, just as the Holy Bible declares God's love for us when it says, “According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love” (Eph 1:4). In His love God knew and sanctified, that is, He set Jeremiah apart to carry out this ministry, that is, to prophesy to His people. This was in the eternal mind of God before the creation of the world. It appears in this verse that Jeremiah is a prophet not only to the Jewish people living in the kingdom of Judah, but to the peoples of the whole world, since he calls them to return to God: “I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

1.3.1.en: God loved you and set you apart to live for Him, and He declared this when you came out of Baptism and were sanctified by the Holy Myron. So do not be distracted from Him by the concerns of the world, or turn away from Him through many sins, for you are consecrated to Him; please Him in everything and serve Him faithfully.

1.4.0.en: Jeremiah felt the greatness of the responsibility of the ministry, and in humility he declared his inability to carry it out, since he was young, so he said, “I am a child.” What is meant by a child is one younger than thirty years, for the Jews considered a man to be mature only when he had passed the age of thirty, which is why Christ began His ministry at this age.

1.4.1.en: It is good to know your weakness, so that you do not rush into any work but count the cost, and declare your weakness before God so that He supports you.

1.5.0.en: God encouraged him so that he would not make an excuse because of his young age, and promised to be with him and to deliver him from the hands of the wicked if they opposed him, until he completed his ministry.

1.6.0.en: God was not content to support Jeremiah with promises, but stretched out His hand and touched his lips, giving him the power to speak the word of God, so that Jeremiah would no longer speak ordinary human words but would utter the powerful and profound word of God. We do not know the form in which God stretched out His hand and touched Jeremiah's mouth. Did a hand appear and touch him? Or did he only feel someone touching his mouth? Or did a light appear before him? In any case, Jeremiah felt a tangible touch on his mouth while he was hearing these words from God.

1.7.0.en: God gave Jeremiah authority over the kingdoms and peoples about whom he would prophesy, such as the kingdom of Judah, Babylon and Philistia, so that he might rebuke their evils until they repent, and thus root out evil from them, pull it down and destroy it, and at the same time build up their spiritual life by the word of God and plant faith in them. In this he is a type of the incarnate Christ, who uproots evil from the souls of those who receive His word, and builds up faith and life with Him in them.

1.7.1.en: Speak with authority when you proclaim the word of God, so that you call everyone to life with Him. Do not be troubled by the opposition of the wicked or their mockery. With the gentleness of love, let your speech be definite and strong, and know that they are troubled however much they oppose you, because the word is not from you but from God.

1.8.s.en: (3) The vision of the almond rod and the swollen pot

1.8.0.en: Rod: the stem of the almond plant.

1.8.1.en: The first vision that God revealed to Jeremiah is the rod of the almond plant. This plant is planted in winter and appears to have no life in it, but before the beginning of spring, that is, in the month of February, it puts forth white blossoms that turn into almond fruit. So the plant seems to be without fruit throughout the winter, but afterwards it gives sweet fruit in the spring. This shows how God watches over and cares for this plant throughout the winter and gives it sweet fruit in the spring. It is worth mentioning that the Hebrew word translated “almond” also means “watcher.”

1.9.0.en: I will hasten: I will carry it out, for the word of God is true and must be fulfilled.

1.9.1.en: God praised Jeremiah because he understood and discerned the almond rod that he saw, and He interpreted the meaning of the vision to him, which is God's watchfulness and concern for the effect of His word on people. God is long-suffering, but at the right time He carries out everything: He punishes the children of Israel for their sins with captivity, and He also punishes those whom He used to punish them, namely the kingdom of Babylon, by the destruction of their kingdom at the hands of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians.

1.9.2.en: The almond fruit has a green outer covering that falls away with time, and then a strong dry shell which, when broken, reveals within it the sweet fruit that is eaten. In the same way, the word of God does not reach its sweetness except after we endure bitter striving and severe pains to break the powers of evil, but in the end we must taste its sweet effect in our lives.

1.9.3.en: Those who are far from God claim that the world goes on without God's intervention, and consequently they neglect His commandments. But God's long-suffering does not cancel His word, which must be fulfilled; He rewards the righteous and repays the wicked, because He watches over His word to perform it. What is meant here is to warn the people through Jeremiah by this prophecy, so that they obey God and His word, which will be fulfilled, and do not persist in their evil, or else He will punish them with captivity.

1.10.0.en: A swollen pot: a large vessel with a mouth, shaped like a sphere, like the pot used for beans whose belly is swollen. Its face is toward the north: its mouth is turned toward the north.

1.10.1.en: The second vision that Jeremiah saw is a swollen pot, which signifies the pride of the Jews, who thought that as long as the temple of God was among them no harm would come to them, and that as long as they had the outward forms of personal worship they were safe. The mouth of the pot, turned toward the north, signifies the Babylonian attack from the north upon Jerusalem and Judea, and their occupation and destruction.

1.11.0.en: From the north the kingdom of Babylon will arise and attack the surrounding countries of the world and Jerusalem, and will destroy it.

1.12.0.en: His throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem: this means the occupation of the city and control of its gates. Its walls: that is, control of the walls and their destruction.

1.12.1.en: All the cities of Judah: that is, all the lands of the kingdom of Judah, which is the southern kingdom of the Jews. God continues His speech with Jeremiah, saying that the kingdom of Babylon will attack Jerusalem and occupy it, and will also occupy all the lands of the kingdom of Judah, take captive those who are in them, plunder their wealth and destroy them.

1.13.0.en: I will utter my judgments: I will declare My punishment.

1.13.1.en: God explains that the destruction of Jerusalem and Judea and their captivity is a punishment for His people because they worshiped idols and walked in many evils.

1.13.2.en: So God warns His people by the first vision, so that they may repent, and if they do not repent, the second prophecy comes upon them, which is destruction.

1.13.3.en: May you pay attention to the word of God that He sends to you to keep you away from evil and draw you to His love, so that you enjoy peace and are delivered from many troubles. For if you neglect His word, nothing awaits you but anxiety and turmoil in this life, and then eternal torment in the life to come.

1.14.0.en: Gird up thy loins: put on a girdle, that is, a wide belt around the waist. This signifies intensity of work and ministry.

1.14.1.en: God asked Jeremiah to proclaim these visions and their interpretation to the people, and to prepare for the labors of this ministry, and not to fear the people's opposition to him, or their rebuke, or their rejection of his word, or their threats against him. He reminds him that what matters most is the fear of God, not the fear of people.

1.14.2.en: So that Jeremiah would not draw back from his ministry, He warned him that if he neglected his ministry and feared the people, God would make him afraid and punish him. God had to warn Jeremiah in this way because He knew the severity of the opposition he would meet from the wicked, so this warning was to protect him from drawing back.

1.14.3.en: The fear of God keeps you away from sin and helps you hold fast to His commandments and perform His service faithfully, so that you enjoy His care and His love.

1.15.0.en: A defenced city: Jeremiah becomes a support for those who fear God, by his encouragement and care for them, like a fortified city that protects them within it.

1.15.1.en: An iron pillar: that is, a strong foundation upon which the house of God is built, so that he proclaims His word and supports His children. Brasen walls: brass is a strong material, so brazen walls protect those within them, like Jeremiah, to whom God will give strength so that he is not shaken by the doubts and opposition of the wicked.

1.15.2.en: God strengthened Jeremiah with powerful promises that He would make him like a fortified city, a strong iron pillar and brazen walls for everyone who believes and lives with God, and that he himself would stand firm in strength before the wicked. This indeed happened for more than 40 years, during which he rebuked everyone and they opposed him, and he was not shaken until he was martyred in the end.

1.16.0.en: God continued His speech with Jeremiah and made known to him that his people would oppose him and fight against him, but they would not be able to silence him; rather he would remain strong to complete his message and his prophecy, even after they took him against his will to Egypt.

1.16.1.en: Warning Jerusalem so that she may repent

2.0.0.en: Here begin the words of the prophecy that God commanded Jeremiah to speak to the people in Jerusalem, for the words in the first chapter were either commands to Jeremiah as a servant, or visions that he proclaims to the people. In God's speech with His people here, the following appears:

2.0.1.en: 1- That it is a rebuke of love, whispered in the ears of His bride whom He loved, the ears of Jerusalem, since He regards Jerusalem and her people as a bride whom He loves very much.

2.0.2.en: If you notice something wrong in one of your loved ones, rebuke him gently between you and him. Praise him first before you show his faults, encourage him to overcome them, and show him your attachment to him and your trust in him, so that you win his heart; for if you do not win him first, he will not allow you to criticize him.

2.0.4.en: God commends Jerusalem, that is, His people the children of Israel, for their holy zeal toward Him when they left the worship of idols in Egypt and worshiped Him alone in the wilderness of Sinai. This is the zeal of Jerusalem in her youth, before she dwelt in the Promised Land.

2.0.6.en: He compares Jerusalem to a bride whom He betrothed to Himself, and how she loved Him by her worship of Him in the Tabernacle of Meeting at Sinai. She was His betrothed at Sinai, then she became His bride by continuing her worship of Him in Canaan and in the temple of Solomon.

2.0.7.en: 4- Thou wentest after me in the wilderness:

2.0.8.en: This means the children of Israel leaving Egypt with all its good things and going out into the barren wilderness of Sinai, where nothing is sown, in order to worship God far from the idols of Egypt.

2.0.9.en: It is noted here that God commends His people and focuses on their virtues, forgetting their faults in this period, such as murmuring and disobedience.

2.1.0.en: God shows His love for Jerusalem and her place with Him by what He says about her:

2.1.1.en: 1- Holiness unto the LORD: all the children of Israel are the people of God, like Aaron, who was consecrated to his ministry and who put a plate of gold on his turban with “Holiness to the LORD” written on it. They are His people and He cares for them with His love.

2.1.2.en: 2- The firstfruits of his increase: the Law commanded the people of God to offer Him the firstfruits, that is, the first of the harvests. The children of Israel are the first of the peoples who believed and lived for God, to be the firstfruits of the whole world when people from every place believe in Christ. So it is a privilege for Jerusalem to enjoy clinging to God before the other peoples.

2.1.3.en: 3- All that devour him shall offend: if the children of Israel sin and God allows the Gentiles, such as the kingdom of Assyria and Babylon, to take them captive, this is a discipline for Israel; but at the same time God is not pleased with the evil of the Gentiles who wrong His people, and He punishes them with destruction, as happened to Assyria and then Babylon.

2.2.0.en: God directs His prophetic speech to all the Jews in:

2.2.1.en: 1- The house of Jacob: that is, the kingdom of Judah, whose capital is Jerusalem.

2.2.2.en: 2- All the families of the house of Israel: the rest of the tribes who formed the northern kingdom, which Assyria then took captive; some of them remained in the kingdom of Israel, and others were scattered throughout the world by the Assyrians.

2.2.3.en: So the speech is directed to the people of God in every place and time.

2.3.1.en: After vanity: after the vain idols that they worshiped.

2.3.2.en: Became vain: they walked in lusts and sins that profit nothing.

2.3.3.en: God rebukes His people because He did not wrong them, but cared for them with His love, and yet they left Him and worshiped idols and plunged into evil lusts.

2.4.0.en: The shadow of death: the people were exposed to the dangers of death, whether at the hands of enemies or of wild beasts, but God kept them and defended them.

2.4.1.en: The people of God forgot His power that delivered them from the slavery of Egypt by the ten plagues and the parting of the Red Sea, and how He cared for them with manna and quail and water from the rock, shaded them with the cloud and guided them by the pillar of fire by night, although no human being can live in the wilderness of Sinai because of its dryness and the impossibility of life there, especially for a great people numbering about 2 million; and He fought for them against enemies such as Amalek.

2.5.0.en: An abomination: unclean through the worship of idols, with which they defiled the Promised Land.

2.5.1.en: God brought His people into the fertile land of Canaan, filled with orchards of fruit and every good thing, and they ate and were filled, but they turned away from God by worshiping idols, and so they defiled the land that God had cleansed for them.

2.5.2.en: God is ready to keep you in afflictions however hard they may be, and to provide for you in them as He provided for His people in the barren wilderness of Sinai, and then to give you many spiritual good things in the Church, so that you may be filled with them and not defile them with your evil thoughts, your outward worship or your pride. Do not repay God's love with evil, but keep His commandments and thank Him for His gifts.

2.6.0.en: Here God shows the turning away from Him of all the groups of the people, who are:

2.6.1.en: 1- The priests: they performed the rite outwardly and did not bind the people to the love of God and to repentance from their sins.

2.6.2.en: 2- They that handle the law: these are the spiritual teachers who were occupied with other things than the worship of God, and consequently did not teach the people, but taught them teachings that turned them away from God.

2.6.3.en: 3- The pastors: that is, the leaders and kings who were proud and did not keep the commandments of God, and so led the people astray after them into many sins.

2.6.4.en: 4- The prophets: instead of prophesying the word of God, they became false prophets who prophesied for pagan gods such as “Baal,” so their prophecies were mistaken and misleading to the people.

2.6.5.en: From this appears the difficulty of the spiritual situation, since all the groups of the people had turned aside, and no one was left but Jeremiah to proclaim the voice of God.

2.7.0.en: God calls His people in Jerusalem and all of Judea to stand before the court, and He becomes an adversary to them, bringing His case against them, and not only against them but also against their children, because they taught their children evil.

2.8.1.en: Kedar: tribes that dwell in the Arabian Peninsula.

2.8.2.en: God calls the nations of the world as witnesses against His people, whether those in the north-west, such as the island of Crete, or in the south, such as the tribes of Kedar, who worship their pagan gods and do not exchange them for unknown gods; but the people of God changed their true God and worshiped what are no gods, namely the idols, which do not profit them at all but harm them, deprive them and separate them from God.

2.9.2.en: God bears witness against His people, not only the pagan nations but also nature, represented by heaven, and so He calls on the heavens to be amazed, to tremble and to be bewildered at the strange and unreasonable conduct of His people in worshiping idols; and by this they fell into two great sins, which are:

2.9.3.en: 1- They forsook God, the source of their life, without whom they cannot live, for He is like a fountain of living waters by the work of His Holy Spirit in them.

2.9.4.en: 2- They sought another support to rely on in their lives, namely the useless pagan gods, which He compares to broken cisterns from which the water leaks out so that they become dry; however many cisterns of this kind a person digs, he finds no water to quench his thirst, but finds only mud and sand, and his life is made dirty by them. The heavens also signify the angels, who bear witness against His people for turning away from their God and running after idols that do not profit, so that they spend their effort all their lives in vain.

2.9.5.en: Do not waste your time on useless viewing or discussions and neglect your relationship with God, that is, your prayers, your reading and your attachment to the Church, for you will be wearied and lose God's love and care.

2.10.0.en: God asks a rhetorical question about His people, saying: is he a servant to those who humiliate him, whether Egypt or Babylon? That is, did Egypt or Babylon buy him as a servant, or is he a homeborn slave, the son of a servant born in his master's house? In both cases he is a slave, whether his master bought him or he was born in his house. The proof that He offers is that the people of God have become a prey over which their enemies rule. By this He rebukes them: why have they become slaves to the nations that exploit them? The reason, of course, is their distance from God and their falling into many sins, so it is a call to repentance and return to God.

2.11.0.en: Roared: the sound of lions and young lions.

2.11.1.en: He compares the attack of Egypt, Assyria and Babylon on the children of Israel to the roaring of young lions, preparing to pounce on their prey and then attacking, so that they laid waste their land and burned their cities with fire.

2.12.0.en: Noph and Tahapanes: cities of Egypt, used to stand for all of Egypt.

2.12.1.en: Have broken the crown of thy head: have broken your head.

2.12.2.en: God continues His rebuke of the humiliation of His people and the attack of their enemies upon them like young lions, and adds that Egypt has broken the head of His people, that is, shattered their strength and humiliated them.

2.13.0.en: God declares that the reason for all these calamities is their forsaking His worship along the way of their life, and their preoccupation with lusts and the worship of idols, and that this turning aside was by the will of His people and no one forced them to it, so all these troubles came upon them.

2.14.0.en: Sihor: the river full of silt, that is, the river Nile in Egypt.

2.14.1.en: The river: what is meant by it is the river Euphrates, which is in Babylon.

2.14.2.en: God rebukes His people for their resorting to Egypt, which is represented by the waters of the Nile, or their resorting to Babylon, which is represented by the river Euphrates, when it would have been better for them in their distress to resort to God and not to human beings. Egypt signifies fertility and good things, that is, material lusts, while Babylon signifies pride because of its boasting in its greatness.

2.15.0.en: God affirms that the reason for the humiliation and ruin that His people will suffer is their sin and their disobedience to God, their lack of fear of Him, their persisting in their evils and their worship of strange gods. God declares His power by saying that His name is the LORD of hosts; it is He who allowed their humiliation so that they would repent, and He is able to humiliate them and also able to deliver them if they repent.

2.15.1.en: Do not be lax with your sins that you have grown accustomed to, or accept strange sins that the world offers you, so that you anger God and ruin your soul. Do not forget the fear of Him and the torment that awaits you if you persist in this evil. Return quickly, for He loves you and is ready to accept your repentance and to lift from you all these troubles that you brought upon yourself. Temporary pleasure leaves bitterness within you, so do not be deceived by it.

2.16.0.en: Thy yoke: a crosswise piece of wood placed on the necks of animals, from which another piece of wood extends, at the end of which is the agricultural implement, and it is tied to the necks of the animals by a rope; so it represents the weight and the toil that animals bear in pulling agricultural implements.

2.16.1.en: Hill: a mound where they offer worship to idols.

2.16.2.en: God compares His people to animals that people exploited to do their work. God broke the bonds of their servitude when they were in Egypt and gave them freedom to worship Him in the wilderness of Sinai, and then in Canaan, but they returned and enslaved themselves to the pagan gods that they worshiped on the hills or under the shade of trees. He calls idol worship harlotry, because His people, like a bride, turned away from her bridegroom and clung to another, the idol; this is spiritual adultery. Idol worship was also often tied to bodily adultery in order to please the gods.

2.17.0.en: Noble vine: the finest kind of vine.

2.17.3.en: God rebukes His people and compares them to a grapevine of the finest kinds, which God planted when He taught them the truth in the wilderness of Sinai by His commandments and laws. How then did they turn aside from Him and become a strange vine that bears bad fruit? That is, why did they leave His worship and walking in the truth for the worship of idols and walking in evil?!

2.18.0.en: Nitre: an alkaline salt found in the earth mixed with dust, used like soap for cleaning, and extracted from the soap plant.

2.18.1.en: Soap: a plant whose ashes, when burned, become suitable for cleaning like good soap.

2.18.2.en: God rebukes Jerusalem, saying that her concern for the outward forms of worship, or for outward displays of greatness and morals, will not profit her at all; all kinds of cleansing agents, of which the best known are nitre and soap, will not remove her sin from her, because it is engraved on stone before God and cannot be erased except by repentance and returning to Him.

2.19.0.en: The valley: the valley of Hinnom, in which they offer human sacrifices to the pagan gods, that is, their children, to please the idols.

2.19.1.en: Dromedary: the female camel, whose nature is to move lightly to the right and to the left, so it signifies being carried away after strange gods.

2.19.2.en: Hyena: the female hyena, which digs in the ground to eat rotting corpses, so it signifies seeking evil and base lusts.

2.19.3.en: Jerusalem denied her worship of idols and her defilement by them, so God answers her, bearing witness against her to what she did in the valley of Hinnom by offering her children as sacrifices to the pagan gods. He compares her to a camel running to the right and to the left after the pagan gods, and to a hyena in her search for defiled lusts.

2.20.1.en: The wild ass: the wild donkey.

2.20.2.en: Used to the wilderness: running in every direction in the desert, and it signifies the female running after every man.

2.20.3.en: Snuffeth up the wind: an expression of the uselessness of all she does, for she does not breathe in a beautiful fragrance, but wind that has no scent.

2.20.4.en: In her occasion: in her searching like the hyena for dead corpses, which signifies seeking base lusts. Weary themselves: grow tired.

2.20.5.en: In her month: the months suitable for mating among animals.

2.20.6.en: God also compares Jerusalem to the female wild ass that is used to running in the desert, that is, she runs after the pagan gods of the surrounding nations; and when she persists in her lust she is never satisfied, but is as if she were sniffing the wind, and she searches like the hyena for dead corpses, that is, she runs after satisfying her evil lusts. She is like the harlot, whom none who seek her need weary themselves to find, because she offers herself to him and is ready for adultery throughout the period of mating, that is, the months of mating. By this God rebukes her for running after the worship of idols and her constant seeking of defiled lusts.

2.21.0.en: There is no hope: she rejected God's warning and His admonition.

2.21.1.en: He continues to compare her to the harlot who runs barefoot after every man and has become thirsty for a lust of which she is never satisfied. For sin makes a person lose his dignity, that is, the wearing of shoes, and makes him never satisfied, but he feels deprivation and the increasing burning of lust within him.

2.21.2.en: But when God warned Jerusalem of barefootedness and thirst, she rejected His word and declared shamelessly her love of adultery with every stranger; this applies to the various idol worships, and likewise to the persistence in lusts and adultery that was tied to these worships and spread in their lives.

2.22.0.en: He compares them to the thief who delights in what he steals, but whose shame is great when he is caught. So it is, not only with the people in Jerusalem, but also with all their groups, whether the priests, or the kings, or the prophets.

2.23.0.en: A stock: idols made of wood, that is, stems or sticks of plants.

2.23.1.en: A stone: idols made of stones.

2.23.2.en: The people of God persisted in their sins, and worshiped idols made of wood or stones and called them fathers and mothers and protectors for themselves to keep them in their lives; and by this they left God and gave Him their backs. And when they fall into trials and their pagan gods do not help them, they ask God to deliver them, forgetting that they rebelled and disobeyed Him, so they know Him only because of their need.

2.24.0.en: God mocks them and says to them: call upon your pagan gods, which have become very many, as many as the cities of the kingdom of Judah, since each city chose for itself one or more of the pagan gods. He says to them: seek them to save you if they can, and of course they have no power, because they are merely statues.

2.25.0.en: God continues His rebuke of them because they stood as adversaries to Him and disobeyed Him by their worship of the pagan gods.

2.26.0.en: God declares with sorrow that discipline does not profit them, for they did not return to God in repentance. When He sent His prophets to them to rebuke them for their evils, they rose against them and killed them with the sword or in some other way, so they were like lions devouring the righteous prophets whom God sent to bring them back to Him.

2.26.1.en: Do not resist God's warnings and rebukes to you that come to you through your father of confession, or your guides, or all those around you, for He wants your salvation. Obey His commandments, submit to His Church and humble yourself before everyone, and you will find your rest and your salvation.

2.27.0.en: God continues His rebuke of His people who rejected His word, and asks in protest about the reason for their distance from Him, saying: have I been to you a dry, barren wilderness without life, or a land of very great darkness? And why have you wandered, that is, gone far from Me and refused to return to Me? For I was always a light and life to you, as I cared for you in the wilderness of Sinai and in Canaan.

2.28.0.en: God declares that He is the ornament of His people and the garments of righteousness that clothe them. It is reasonable for a bride to care for her ornaments and her attire, that is, her clothing and everything connected with it that is worn around the waist; so why has Jerusalem, as the bride of God, forgotten her Bridegroom, who is her ornament and her splendor?

2.29.0.en: He rebukes Jerusalem that she seeks after the worship of idols as a bride seeks the one she loves, or as the harlot seeks those who desire her and whom she loves. Jerusalem sought evil love, that is, the love of idol worship and base lusts, and even taught her sons and daughters this evil; and by the wicked women is meant her daughters.

2.30.0.en: He adds another sin found in Jerusalem, which is injustice, which He expresses as the blood of the souls of the poor innocents. The sins of Jerusalem are plain and need no digging or searching, but are visible in all her houses and streets.

2.31.0.en: The evil of Jerusalem increased in that she did not confess her sins but tried to justify herself, and claimed that she was innocent of all evil, and that for this reason God had not punished her until now. Therefore God answers her that she ... that God will judge her and punish her.

2.32.0.en: God also rebukes Jerusalem for her running to seek help from Egypt, as she ran in the past to seek help from Assyria, which attacked her, destroyed her cities and took captive the whole northern kingdom. Why then does she run now toward Egypt? So He calls her to repent and return to Him instead of resorting to human beings to deliver her from her calamities, or taking refuge from Babylon, which threatens her.

2.33.0.en: Thine hands upon thine head: in captivity the prisoners go out with their hands on their heads, and this may also happen in the case of intense grief at the death of loved ones.

2.33.1.en: God declares His punishment of Jerusalem for her disobedience: that she will be taken captive and go out of her land as prisoners go out, in intense grief and humiliation, and those in whom she trusted, such as Egypt and Assyria, “thy confidences,” will not profit her. This is what actually happened years later when Babylon attacked and took Jerusalem and Judea captive, because she did not listen to the voice of God through the prophet Jeremiah and did not repent of her sins.

2.33.2.en: Remember that your soul is a bride of Christ, and her joy and her greatness are to cling to Him and to be adorned with the virtues that He gives her. So give enough time to being with God, and remove your sins by repentance, and you will keep your beauty as a bride adorned for her bridegroom.

2.33.3.en: A call to repentance and the hating of sin
